        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 4012e7d09d99b62d80046790657c0b0e32310d50 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alexandre Torgue <alexandre.torgue@st.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Feb 2019 10:49:09 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] net: stmmac: handle endianness in dwmac4_get_timestamp

GMAC IP is little-endian and used on several kind of CPU (big or little
endian). Main callbacks functions of the stmmac drivers take care about
it. It was not the case for dwmac4_get_timestamp function.

Fixes: ba1ffd74df74 ("stmmac: fix PTP support for GMAC4")
Signed-off-by: Alexandre Torgue <alexandre.torgue@st.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
---
 drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c | 9 ++++++---
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c
index 20299f6f65fc..736e29635b77 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_descs.c
@@ -241,15 +241,18 @@ static inline void dwmac4_get_timestamp(void *desc, u32 ats, u64 *ts)
 static int dwmac4_rx_check_timestamp(void *desc)
 {
 	struct dma_desc *p = (struct dma_desc *)desc;
+	unsigned int rdes0 = le32_to_cpu(p->des0);
+	unsigned int rdes1 = le32_to_cpu(p->des1);
+	unsigned int rdes3 = le32_to_cpu(p->des3);
 	u32 own, ctxt;
 	int ret = 1;
 
-	own = p->des3 & RDES3_OWN;
-	ctxt = ((p->des3 & RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR)
+	own = rdes3 & RDES3_OWN;
+	ctxt = ((rdes3 & RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR)
 		>> RDES3_CONTEXT_DESCRIPTOR_SHIFT);
 
 	if (likely(!own && ctxt)) {
-		if ((p->des0 == 0xffffffff) && (p->des1 == 0xffffffff))
+		if ((rdes0 == 0xffffffff) && (rdes1 == 0xffffffff))
 			/* Corrupted value */
 			ret = -EINVAL;
 		else
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the `dwmac4_get_timestamp` function not properly handling endianness when accessing the descriptor fields. The original code was directly using the descriptor values without converting them from little-endian to the host's endianness, which could lead to incorrect interpretations of the data on big-endian systems. The patch fixes this by using the `le32_to_cpu` macro to ensure that the descriptor values are correctly converted before being used.

    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the `dwmac4_get_timestamp` function not properly handling endianness when accessing the descriptor fields. The original code was directly using the descriptor values without converting them from little-endian to the host's endianness, which could lead to incorrect interpretations of the data on big-endian systems. The patch fixes this by using the `le32_to_cpu` macro to ensure that the descriptor values are correctly converted before being used.
